nodes.title: rc2 field feedback: worktrees, workers and the review loop

acceptance: review-packet, review record, handoff status and worker delegate run in a linked worktree all read and write the leaf's review directory at one documented location (the main checkout's work/reviews/<ID>/, as the executor prompt already states); no command reads READY from the worktree while another writes PACKET.md to the main checkout

The reviewer prompt names that directory as the one path the reviewer must be able to write, so a harness sandboxed to the worktree can be launched with it as a writable root; docs/orchestration-review.md says so
A test runs review-packet, review record and handoff status from a linked worktree and shows they agree on the directory
nodes.title: In a git worktree, every command resolves work/ paths the same way and a sandboxed reviewer can file its record

acceptance: worker message W --text ... resumes a worker in state failed or stalled when its record holds a native session id, instead of refusing with 'delegate again'; a failed worker without a session id is still refused with that hint
The resumed turn counts against max_workers like any other launch; docs/orchestration-workers.md lists which states can be resumed
Tests cover resuming a failed worker with and without a session id
nodes.title: worker message resumes a failed or stalled worker whose native session id is known

acceptance: The executor and reviewer clean-tree preconditions and delegation's uncommitted-work check ignore specy-road's own runtime state (work/.workers/ and the other generated work/ bookkeeping), in the main checkout, a linked worktree and a separate clone
init project (and refresh) make sure those runtime paths are ignored by git in a new project, so a fresh clone starts clean
A test delegates in a fresh clone and shows the precondition passes while an unrelated untracked file still fails it
nodes.title: specy-road's own runtime directories never fail the clean-tree checks

acceptance: worker delegate and worker message/resume refuse a launch that would exceed policy.max_workers, counting live workers in the main checkout and in every linked worktree or clone that shares the integration branch's registry
docs/orchestration-workers.md states what is counted and how a separate clone is included (for example through the claims on the integration branch)
Tests show a resume refused at the limit and two checkouts sharing one limit
nodes.title: max_workers counts live workers across checkouts and applies to resumes

acceptance: A claim whose feature branch exists locally is never reported as stale, whether or not the branch has been pushed, so a successful pickup prints no stale-claim warning
The stale-claim warning and its fix lines (abort-task-pickup --force, removing the row) are printed only when neither a local nor a remote feature branch exists, and say which was checked
Tests cover a local-only branch (no warning) and a missing branch (warning)
nodes.title: Pickup's stale-claim check tests the local branch and never advises deleting a live claim

acceptance: worker reconcile compares changed paths with the leaf's current touch zones (the claim row as edit-node now keeps it), not the zones snapshotted at delegation
Paths that arrive only through a merge of the integration branch into the leaf branch are not reported as outside the touch zones
'The leaf's brief changed since delegation' is reported only when the leaf's own contract changed (acceptance, touch zones, sheet), not whenever the integration branch moved; tests cover all three
nodes.title: worker reconcile judges a worker against the leaf's current contract

acceptance: specy-road review delegate <ID> --model <roster id> builds the reviewer prompt, launches the roster entry's harness, records the reviewer's native session id, and can resume it

A provider capacity or rate-limit error is retried with backoff a bounded number of times; a run that ends without a valid record is reported as incomplete for that commit, and handoff status never presents an older commit's record as the current verdict
docs/orchestration-review.md documents the command; tests use a fake harness for success, a capacity error then success, and a run that writes no record
nodes.title: review delegate runs a rostered reviewer like worker delegate runs an executor

acceptance: With a policy setting enabled, review-packet --since-approved builds a packet of the diff since the last commit a reviewer approved, plus that reviewer's notes, when the delta is below a size threshold and touches only paths of the configured kinds (for example docs or tests)
The gate counts such a delta approval only for a reviewer who approved the earlier commit, only under the policy, and full fresh review stays the default
Tests cover an eligible delta, a delta over the threshold, and the policy off
nodes.title: An opt-in delta review packet for small fix rounds

acceptance: An acceptance item can be marked human (for example a 'human:' prefix or a per-item flag in the schema); reviewers are told to mark it n/a with the reason 'human', and the review gate does not count it as a fail
finish-this-task refuses while a human item has no recorded decision on the planning sheet, and says how to record it
docs/roadmap-authoring.md documents the marker; tests cover a reviewer skip and the finish refusal
nodes.title: Acceptance items a human must satisfy are marked and handled as such

acceptance: edit-node --add touch_zones=<path> and --remove touch_zones=<path> change one entry without restating the list; the same works for dependencies and acceptance
The claim row follows as it does for --set (M10.14); tests cover add, remove, a duplicate add and removing a missing entry
nodes.title: edit-node can add and remove single list entries

acceptance: A leaf that pickup would skip (for example a scaffold sheet with no acceptance) is not listed as ready by orchestrate plan or grind-session --plan; all three call one readiness function
orchestrate plan ranks executor candidates using roster class and billing_route when cost data is unknown, instead of always choosing one model
Tests show the three commands agree on a fixture, and a roster with cheap and senior classes is ranked accordingly
nodes.title: orchestrate plan, grind-session --plan and pickup share one readiness rule and rank executors by class and billing route

acceptance: specy-road ready <ID> --verify '<cmd>=<exit>' ... writes READY-<model>.md in the leaf's review directory with valid front matter and the current commit, and refuses a non-zero verifier unless it is marked as red-green evidence
The executor prompt tells executors to write READY with this command; handoff status still validates hand-written files
Tests cover a valid write, a refused failing verifier, and the prompt text
nodes.title: specy-road ready writes a valid READY hand-off
